subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK single-tool invoke and command cron, and what security gates are mandatory for host filesystem, process, session, CLI, and startup-readiness paths?
rationale: The remaining work changes privileged execution and filesystem boundaries, so automation cannot choose between keeping the core surface narrow, landing explicit opt-ins, or approving a broader direct-execution design.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Use this issue to track maintainer-reviewed PRs that add one direct-invoke capability at a time with explicit opt-ins, owner checks, audit coverage, docs, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Limit scope to shipped invoke paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK single-tool invoke plus command cron sufficient and close remaining host-FS, exec, session, and CLI direct-dispatch work as out of scope for core.

options.title: Approve a broader direct-execution design
options.body: Accept a larger core design that exposes more tools directly, but require a security design review before implementation continues.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue to track maintainer-reviewed PRs that add one direct-invoke capability at a time with explicit opt-ins, owner checks, audit coverage, docs, and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a Gateway security boundary and recent history points to this owner area.
